{
  "dataset_name": "bank_marketing",
  "model_family": "tree",
  "schema_generator": "claude-sonnet-4.6",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "duration_log",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Log-transformed call duration to compress right skew and create better split points for tree models",
      "value_range": [0.0, 8.35],
      "feature_family": "call_engagement",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Nonlinear transformation allows tree to find meaningful thresholds in compressed duration space",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.log1p(duration)"
    },
    {
      "name": "previously_contacted",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Binary indicator whether client was contacted in a previous campaign (pdays < 999 means they were contacted)",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "campaign_history",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Direct boolean split on prior contact history which strongly differentiates client engagement",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(pdays < 999, 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "campaign_intensity",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ordinal bucket of number of contacts during current campaign: 1=single, 2=low(2-3), 3=medium(4-6), 4=high(7+)",
      "value_range": [1, 4],
      "feature_family": "campaign_history",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Ordinal grouping reduces noise from raw campaign count and provides direct split points",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(campaign == 1, 1, np.where(campaign <= 3, 2, np.where(campaign <= 6, 3, 4)))"
    },
    {
      "name": "economic_stress_index",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Combined economic stress signal: high euribor3m and high employment rate indicate tighter economic conditions",
      "value_range": [0.0, 7.0],
      "feature_family": "macroeconomic",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Interaction between interest rates and employment captures macro environment better than individual features",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.clip(euribor3m, 0.0, 5.0) + np.clip((nr.employed - 5000.0) / 50.0, 0.0, 2.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "age_bucket",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Age grouped into life-stage buckets: 1=young(17-30), 2=early-career(31-40), 3=mid-career(41-55), 4=pre-retirement(56-65), 5=retired(66+)",
      "value_range": [1, 5],
      "feature_family": "demographics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Life-stage grouping captures nonlinear age effects on financial product subscription likelihood",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(age <= 30, 1, np.where(age <= 40, 2, np.where(age <= 55, 3, np.where(age <= 65, 4, 5))))"
    },
    {
      "name": "debt_burden_flag",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Binary flag indicating client has both housing loan and personal loan (double debt burden)",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "financial_obligations",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Interaction of two loan indicators captures clients with highest financial obligations who may resist new products",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where((housing == 1) & (loan == 1), 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "recency_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Inverse recency of last contact: 0 if never contacted, else scaled score where lower pdays means more recent",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "campaign_history",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures recency effect of prior campaigns; recent contacts may have warmer leads",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(pdays >= 999, 0.0, np.clip(1.0 - pdays / 30.0, 0.0, 1.0))"
    },
    {
      "name": "favorable_macro_env",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Binary flag for favorable macroeconomic environment: low euribor3m (<2.0) and negative emp.var.rate indicating easing conditions",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "macroeconomic",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Boolean split on macro conditions that historically correlate with higher subscription rates",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where((euribor3m < 2.0) & (emp.var.rate < 0.0), 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "prior_success_indicator",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Flag for clients with successful previous campaign outcome (poutcome == 1 typically maps to success) and at least one prior contact",
      "value_range": [0, 1],
      "feature_family": "campaign_history",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Prior campaign success is a strong predictor of current subscription; direct boolean split",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where((poutcome == 1) & (previous > 0), 1, 0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "education_job_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Product of education level and job category to capture socioeconomic profile interactions",
      "value_range": [0.0, 77.0],
      "feature_family": "demographics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Interaction term captures combined socioeconomic status effects that neither feature captures alone",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "education * job"
    },
    {
      "name": "contact_receptiveness",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Semantic score assessing how receptive a client profile is to contact based on job stability, marital status, and education level. Higher scores indicate profiles historically more open to financial product discussions. Score 1=low receptiveness (unstable job, low education), 5=high receptiveness (professional, high education, single or married).",
      "value_range": [1, 5],
      "feature_family": "demographics",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures latent receptiveness signal from demographic combination that individual features miss",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "financial_stability_score",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Semantic assessment of financial stability based on default status, loan burden, and job type. Score 1=very unstable (has default, multiple loans, unstable job), 5=very stable (no default, no loans, professional/management job). Captures overall financial health profile.",
      "value_range": [1, 5],
      "feature_family": "financial_obligations",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Holistic financial stability assessment provides tree with a pre-computed stability axis for splitting",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
